title: Zero-sum marketing channels: why startups should invest in non-zero-sum channels instead
summary: Jason Cohen argues that channels like AdWords and top-ranking SEO are zero-sum: winners lock out others, cost top dollar, and are capped in volume. Startups are better off investing in non-zero-sum channels like social, content, long-tail SEO and resellers, where success depends on yourself and the ceiling is the market itself.

principles.text: Zero-sum channels (AdWords, top SEO slots) mean winning costs top dollar for capped inventory.
principles.quote: So, even if you win a zero-sum channel, your growth in that channel is capped, and expensive.

principles.text: Invest in non-zero-sum channels, where the limit is the market itself, not one ad platform's slice of it.
principles.quote: Whereas if you invest in non-zero-sum channels like social media, long-tail SEO, brand-building, content, value-added resellers, or even cold-calling, the limit of the channel is closer to the limit of the market itself

principles.text: Prefer channels where success depends on you, not on a platform's rules or a competitor's willingness to burn money.
principles.quote: your success is dependent almost exclusively on yourself, not dependent on how some advertising platform works, or how much money some competitor is willing lose.

principles.text: Small companies can't outspend big or funded ones in zero-sum fights, but big players can't stop you winning elsewhere.
principles.quote: there's nothing the big guys can do to prevent you from shining in the other games.

principles.text: Focus on the few things a startup controls: product, culture and your voice online.
principles.quote: There are few things in startups that you control. The product, your culture, and your voice online are among the few
